overall: Okay so fun wins for me because it sounds like my group chat without trying to be my group chat. Texting a few memes and calling the rest of the day mine, a week in my cart, the notes app being full, replies getting slower and slower, saying "Obsessed." about a bad haircut: I have actually done all of that, and none of the answers make me look good or bad, so I'd just answer honestly. Callout has the best single lines ("Still annoyed about my salad", "Twice. They were alive.", "It'll grow on me! It won't.") and I'd screenshot those, but sometimes the jab tips an answer into the fun rebel pick ("Oops") or sounds like an adult doing a bit ("Yawns quietly", food pics). Scenario is close behind: the little moments ("can you talk tonight?", the bill landing between you) pull me in, but then it says brunch and roommates and I remember it wasn't written for me. Quest is fine when it's plain and cringe when it isn't: "side quest", "daily tasks" and "level up" are exactly what I mean by adults trying to sound young, and I play Minecraft every day. Kind is the clearest and weirdly the fairest (it's the only one where helping people isn't the automatic good-kid answer), but it reads like a guidance counselor wrote it, so I'd never send it to anyone. Oracle loses me by question three. The cards seeing me, recalling me and replaying my group chat drama gets old fast, and putting "The stars align" on the getting-physical question and a fortune teller on a sick relative is just uncomfortable. Also, a lot of these (marriage, kids, wedding, getting physical, rent, buying a house) are not my life at all, so none of them could get a high share from me no matter who wrote them.
